content.text: {"primary_meaning":"There is no settled, independent Christian symbolic meaning for Hebrew kaph (“palm,” “hollow of the hand”). When it is treated symbolically, its broadest recurring association is the hand as an image of protective care, sustaining possession, or secure holding—especially God’s care—though the meaning is determined by each passage rather than by kaph itself.","primary_basis":["Isaiah 49:16 — Zion is engraved on the palms of God’s hands, commonly interpreted as continual remembrance and covenant care.","Exodus 33:22 — God covers Moses with his palm/hand, providing protection in the divine presence.","Psalm 139:5 — God lays his hand upon the psalmist, suggesting encompassing presence, care, or restraint.","Isaiah 40:12 — God measures the waters in the hollow of his hand, portraying sovereign power and control over creation.","John 10:28–29 — although Greek and not a lexical use of kaph, being held in the Father’s and Son’s hand is often associated thematically with divine security."] ,"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Power, authority, agency, or ability to act. This is a widespread symbolism of “hand” generally, but it is not distinctive to kaph and often rests on other Hebrew hand-terms such as yad or on “right hand” imagery.","basis":["Isaiah 40:12 — creation measured in the hollow of God’s hand.","Exodus 9:3 — the hand of the Lord as active divine power, though the Hebrew term is yad rather than kaph.","Psalm 118:15–16 — the Lord’s right hand as power and victory, again using broader hand imagery."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Remembrance, personal inscription, or belonging to God.","basis":["Isaiah 49:16 — “I have engraved you on the palms of my hands,” interpreted as unfailing remembrance and attachment."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Prayer, worship, surrender, or dependence, represented by opened or uplifted palms.","basis":["Psalm 63:4 — lifting the hands in blessing or worship.","Psalm 141:2 — uplifted hands compared with the evening sacrifice.","1 Timothy 2:8 — lifting holy hands in prayer; Greek rather than Hebrew kaph."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Giving, receiving, generosity, or openness, based on the open palm as the bodily means of offering or receiving.","basis":["Deuteronomy 15:8 — opening the hand generously to the poor, although the principal Hebrew hand-term is yad.","Proverbs 31:20 — opening the hand to the poor and extending help to the needy; both kaph and yad occur in the verse."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Human work, deeds, conduct, or responsibility—the “work of one’s hands.” This is common biblical hand imagery but is not specifically tied to the palm.","basis":["Psalm 90:17 — establishing the work of human hands.","Proverbs 31:31 — praise arising from the works of one’s hands.","Ecclesiastes 9:10 — doing whatever one’s hand finds to do."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"A letter-symbol interpretation in which the Hebrew letter kaph signifies an open or curved hand and therefore receiving, submission, covering, or crowning.","basis":["The pictorial shape or proposed ancient pictographic background of the Hebrew letter kaph.","Occasional Christian alphabetic, devotional, and messianic symbolism rather than standard contextual exegesis."],"prominence":"rare"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"Kaph is primarily a lexical term for the palm or hollow of the hand and can also denote similarly shaped objects, such as a spoon or bowl, and sometimes the sole of the foot. Biblical writers use it in several different images. Christian interpretation has a recognizable general symbolism of the hand—care, power, agency, prayer, giving, and possession—but no single symbolic definition of kaph commands a settled consensus."}
